A.explanation: Amplitude is the maximum displacement. The dashed lines show the peaks stay at the same displacement, so amplitude is constant.

B.explanation: The time for each oscillation gets shorter along the time axis, so period decreases and frequency $f = 1/T$ increases.

C.explanation: Period is the time for one complete oscillation. Successive cycles occupy less time, so period is decreasing, not increasing.

D.explanation: Wave speed $v = f\lambda$ is set by the medium for sound and cannot be found from a single particle displacement-time graph alone.

hints: Look at the two horizontal dashed lines for peak displacement and at the spacing of the peaks along the time axis.
Recall that maximum displacement gives amplitude and time for one full up-down cycle gives period $T$, with frequency $f = 1/T$.
Compare the first long oscillation with the later faster oscillations to decide which of amplitude, $T$ and $f$ stays the same and which changes.
walkthrough: Identify what the graph shows: vertical axis is displacement of one air particle, horizontal axis is time, so it is vibration of the source repeated in time.
Read amplitude: the highest and lowest points just touch the same upper and lower dashed lines throughout, so maximum displacement $x_0$ is unchanged.
Read period: $T$ is the time between the same point on successive cycles, for example peak to peak. The second and third peaks are closer together in time than the start of the motion.
Apply $f = 1/T$: a shorter $T$ means more oscillations per unit time, so frequency must be increasing.
Speed of sound depends on properties of air, not on this timing change shown for one particle, so it is not forced to increase. This is option B.
